c: FreshWay Market, a three-store grocery chain
s: FreshWay Market throws away a large amount of produce and dairy each week, while some shelves run empty on weekends. A customer recently became ill after buying a product that was past its sell-by date.
The operations director (judge) wants you to explain how the store can improve ordering and stock rotation, what quality control and food safety measures it needs, and how to reduce waste.
p: Describe health and safety regulations in business
Explain the concept of supply chain
n: First-in, first-out rotation and date checks
Uses sales data to set order quantities and reorder points
Temperature logs, inspections and training
Knows food safety rules and how to remove items promptly
Supply chain: grower, distributor, store, customer, and why timely delivery matters
q: A customer reports illness after buying an item from your store. What do you do?
How would you reduce waste without running out of stock?

c: Harvest Table, a farm-to-table grocery and prepared foods store
s: Harvest Table is introducing a line of locally made sauces and wants shoppers to try them. The company wants to use in-store demonstrations, social media and local partnerships without a large advertising budget.
The marketing manager (judge) wants you to explain how to promote the new line, how to use in-store events and publicity, and how to keep the message consistent.
p: Identify communications channels used in sales promotion
Explain the nature of word-of-mouth (WOM) strategies
Coordinate activities in the promotional mix
n: Sampling stations, coupons and displays near the entrance
Local media features, producer meet-and-greets and community events
Encourages reviews, photos and sharing
Signage that names the maker, taste and price
Same look and message across store, web and social
q: How would you decide which local food producer to feature first?
What would you do if a sample caused an allergic reaction?

c: Corner Fresh Deli, an upscale deli within a supermarket
s: Corner Fresh Deli sells prepared salads, sandwiches and catered trays. The department manager wants associates to sell more catered trays for office lunches and weekend gatherings, but employees say customers rarely ask about them.
The department manager (judge) wants you to explain how to start a conversation with a customer about catering, how to explain product benefits, and how to close an order.
p: Explain key factors in building a clientele
Process special orders for retail sales
n: Opens with a question about upcoming events
Suggests a tray size, extras and dessert based on guest count
Builds repeat customers through reliability, follow-up and personalization
Explains order lead time, allergen information and payment terms
Records details accurately and confirms pick-up
q: A customer says the catering price is too high. How do you respond?
What would you do if a customer's order was prepared incorrectly?

c: Valley Fresh Foods, a regional supplier of produce to grocery stores
s: Valley Fresh Foods ships produce to forty grocery stores. Delays at the warehouse and weather-related road closures have led to spoiled produce and unhappy store managers.
The distribution manager (judge) wants you to explain how channel decisions affect product quality, how to manage relationships with channel members, and what technology could improve delivery.
p: Explain the nature of channels of distribution
Explain the nature of channel-member relationships
Describe the use of technology in the channel management function
Explain the nature and scope of distribution
n: Describes the path from farm to warehouse to store and the roles of each
Communicates with retailers, shares forecasts and solves problems together
GPS tracking, route software and temperature sensors
Explains the importance of timely and safe delivery for perishable goods
Compares shipping methods by speed, cost and reliability
q: A major store threatens to switch suppliers after a late delivery. What do you do?
How would you decide between a faster, more expensive shipment and a slower, cheaper one?

c: Sprout & Co., a natural foods store with an online ordering service
s: Sprout & Co.'s online grocery orders are often missing items or include substitutions customers did not want. Complaints on social media are growing and some customers are canceling their weekly orders.
The customer service manager (judge) wants you to explain how to respond to the complaints, what a customer service mindset is, and how the store can use technology to improve the experience.
p: Describe the use of technology in customer relationship management
n: Responds quickly, apologizes and offers a refund, credit or replacement
Treats every customer as valued and takes ownership
Answers questions accurately and follows up
Uses order notes, preferences and feedback surveys
Personalizes communication and builds trust
q: A customer says, 'This is the third time my order was wrong.' What do you say?
How would you prevent substitutions customers do not want?
